A skip into node 2 passes stable raw features, so the conv on edge 5 operates on a well-conditioned input and adds capacity without a deep conv stack.
Without the direct input-to-output edge, edge 4 is one of only two routes to the output, so upgrading its capacity matters more.
With a direct 3x3 conv into the output, a pooled route through node 2 contributes mostly blur and dilutes the sum.
With edge 5 removed, the direct edge is one of the few routes carrying input features to the output so giving it a 3x3 conv matters more.
With edge 5 removed, node 1 reaches the output only via edge 4, so its capacity directly determines how much of that branch is used.
With edge 2 removed, node 2 is fed only by edge 1, so its op fully determines node 2's representation.
With edge 1 removed, edge 2 is the only feeder of node 2, so upgrading it matters more than when a parallel route exists.
Without the direct edge, all input information passes through edge 0 or edge 1, so edge 0's quality is a bottleneck.
With edge 4 removed, node 1 information has one fewer route to the output, so a strong direct 3x3 from the input compensates more.
